attributes.body_ja:
「とても〜ない」は、動詞（どうし）の否定形（ひていけい）を含（ふく）む文（ぶん）に、「とても」を付（つ）けた形（かたち）で、「絶対（ぜったい）に (A) はできない」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。「とても」は、不可能（ふかのう）だというときに使（つか）われるので、多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、動詞（どうし）は可能形（かのうけい）になります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

話（はな）し手（て）が「(A) は不可能（ふかのう）だ」と感（かん）じていることがわかる文（ぶん）なら、動詞（どうし）が否定形（ひていけい）である必要（ひつよう）はありません。
attributes.body:
When seen in sentences containing verbs negated with the auxiliary verb ない, とても carries the nuance of 'not (A) at all', or 'cannot (A) at all'. とても is supposed to only be used when expressing 'impossibility', 不可能（ふかのう）. Due to this, it will primarily appear alongside the potential form of verbs.

Fun Fact

As long as some part of the sentence expresses the speaker's view about the impossibility of (A), the verb is not always required to be in the negative form.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both ぜんぜん (with a negative form) and とても～ない can mean 'not at all', but differ slightly in nuance. とても～ない emphasizes impossibility, e.g. とてもできない and ぜんぜんできない both mean 'I absolutely can't do it.'. With adjectives like 美味しくない, where there is no sense of potential, 全然 is preferred, e.g. 全然美味しくない ('It's not tasty at all.').

second_relatable.title: とても～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not ~ at all, Cannot ~ at all

attributes.body: 全く～ない and とても～ない both express strong negation, but differ in nuance. 全く～ない is used to completely deny or negate something, indicating total absence or lack. とても～ない, on the other hand, implies an extreme state or condition that makes something impossible, adding a nuance of implausibility or incapability.

second_relatable.title: とても～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not ~ at all, Cannot ~ at all

attributes.body: とても～ない is an emphatic negative used to show that something is far beyond one's ability. For example, とてもできない ('I can't do that at all.'). In contrast, すこしも～ない means 'not even a little bit (A)' and isn't limited to ability. For example, すこしも面白くない ('It's not interesting at all.'). Unlike すこしも, とても can be used without ない if the meaning is still negative, e.g. とても無理だ ('It's completely impossible.').
